_comment: Filament reference data. Temperatures are nozzle/bed in Celsius. These are working ranges from manufacturer datasheets and established community practice — always defer to the number printed on the spool, which is why every material page says so. Add a material by copying a block and changing the values; nothing in the code needs to be touched.

pla.name: PLA
pla.summary: The default. Easiest to print, lowest warping, poor heat resistance. If a part will sit in a car in summer, do not use PLA.
pla.enclosureNote: An enclosure raises chamber temperature and softens PLA before it finishes cooling. Leave the door open.
watchFor: Softening in hot cars or direct sun — it starts moving around 60 °C
Brittleness after months of UV exposure

pla-plus.name: PLA+
pla-plus.summary: PLA with toughening additives. Slightly higher temperatures, noticeably less brittle, otherwise behaves like PLA.
pla-plus.enclosureNote: Same as PLA — keep the chamber cool.
watchFor: Brand-to-brand variation is much wider than with plain PLA — re-tune when you switch supplier

petg.name: PETG
petg.summary: Tougher and more heat resistant than PLA, and the usual first step up. Strings enthusiastically and sticks to smooth beds hard enough to damage them.
petg.enclosureNote: Helps a little with layer adhesion, not required.
watchFor: Bonds to bare smooth PEI so strongly it can tear the sheet — use textured PEI or a glue-stick release layer
Absorbs moisture from the air within days; wet PETG pops and strings far worse than dry

abs.name: ABS
abs.summary: Heat resistant and machinable, but it warps hard and needs a warm, still chamber. Not a material to print in an open printer in a cold room.
abs.enclosureNote: Draughts cause layer splitting. The chamber needs to be warm and, more importantly, still.
watchFor: Emits styrene while printing — ventilate the room, do not sit next to it
Large flat parts will lift at the corners no matter how good the first layer is; design in a brim or split the part

asa.name: ASA
asa.summary: ABS with proper UV resistance. The right answer for parts that live outdoors. Prints like ABS and warps like ABS.
asa.enclosureNote: Same as ABS. Still air matters more than hot air.
watchFor: Ventilate as you would for ABS
Holds colour outdoors for years where ABS chalks and yellows

tpu.name: TPU
tpu.summary: Flexible. Prints slowly, hates retraction, and will jam a Bowden setup given the slightest excuse.
watchFor: Print slowly — 15–30 mm/s on most machines. Speed is the single most common cause of TPU failures
Direct drive strongly preferred; softer shore ratings buckle in a Bowden tube

nylon.name: Nylon (PA)
nylon.summary: Tough, abrasion resistant, and a sponge. Nylon straight off a shelf that has been open for a week will print badly no matter what settings you use.
nylon.enclosureNote: Needed for layer adhesion and to keep ambient humidity away from the part.
watchFor: Dry it before every print, not once a month. This is not optional advice
Absorbs moisture fast enough that a long print can degrade partway through — print from a dry box

pc.name: PC
pc.summary: The strongest common filament and the most demanding. High temperatures, high warping, and it needs a machine that can genuinely reach the numbers.
pc.enclosureNote: An actively heated chamber is close to mandatory for parts above a few centimetres.
watchFor: Most stock hotends top out below what PC really wants — check your maximum before buying a spool
Wet PC prints cloudy and weak, and the difference is dramatic

petg-cf.name: PETG-CF
petg-cf.summary: Stiffer and more dimensionally stable than plain PETG, with a matte finish. The carbon fibre will destroy a brass nozzle.
petg-cf.enclosureNote: Helpful for layer adhesion on larger parts.
watchFor: Hardened steel or ruby nozzle required — brass wears out in hours, not weeks
Needs a larger nozzle (0.4 mm minimum, 0.6 mm preferred) or it clogs

pa-cf.name: PA-CF
pa-cf.summary: Engineering-grade: stiff, tough, heat resistant, dimensionally far better behaved than plain nylon. Abrasive and thirsty.
watchFor: Hardened steel nozzle required
Carbon fill reduces warping compared to plain nylon but does nothing about moisture — still dry it every time

hips.name: HIPS
hips.summary: Mostly used as a dissolvable support for ABS, since limonene removes it. Prints similarly to ABS on its own.
watchFor: Ventilate as for ABS
Dissolves in limonene, which takes hours and smells strongly of oranges

pvb.name: PVB
pvb.summary: Prints much like PLA but smooths with isopropyl alcohol vapour, so it is the usual choice for transparent or polished parts.
watchFor: Softens in humidity over time — finished parts are not weatherproof
IPA smoothing works but is flammable; do it away from anything hot
